§. 144. 7. Istæ Traditiones pro Apostolicis haben-

Quando universa Ecclesia cujuscunque ævi Ali-
quid pro Fidei Dogmate amplectitur, & Opposi-
tum pro hæretico damnat, etsi neque expresse in-
veniatur in S. Literis, neque Deductio illius ex

Fide Revelationis post Illorum mortem, vel
præ se fert, vel expectat. Tenet hæc Regula sim-
pliciter, ni forte evidenter oftendi possit aliquod
Dogma, quod Ecclesia Catholica hujus, vel cujus-

vel fuisse plane contrarium S. Scripturæ, aut Ec-

damnasse, quod illa de Fide tenuit. Quod certe
neutiquam probabile, si modo Possibile sit. Secun-

page.notes: The running head reads "De sana, sive recta Ratione." The word "recta" is printed with a worn ligature and could be misread; checked against the image. "Istæ" is read from "Iftæ" with the long-s/t ligature. The final "let," is the catchword for the next page, since it stands alone below the last line and completes "va-". The "Apostolicis" and "Primo"/"Secundo" italic readings are as seen; the scan is faint in places.
